entries.title: Omnibus I published: CSRD scope narrowed to >1,000 employees and >€450m turnover
entries.summary: The Omnibus I directive was published in the Official Journal on 26 Feb 2026 and entered into force on 18 Mar 2026. CSRD now applies to EU undertakings/groups with more than 1,000 employees and more than €450m net turnover. Member states must transpose it by 19 Mar 2027.
entries.whyItMatters: Confirms which reporting obligations remain for us and when national law (DE) will catch up. Check the impact on our reporting timeline and on the data scope we keep in Fabric.

entries.title: CSDDD: scope raised to >5,000 employees and €1.5bn turnover, compliance from July 2029
entries.summary: Through Omnibus I, the CSDDD now covers EU companies with more than 5,000 employees and more than €1.5bn worldwide net turnover. The transposition deadline is 26 Jul 2028, and companies must comply from 26 Jul 2029. Annual due diligence statements apply from FY2030.
entries.whyItMatters: Mainly relevant to check whether we are in scope. Even if we're not, large customers may cascade due diligence data requests to suppliers.

entries.title: Revised ESRS (2026) published in the Official Journal, applies from FY2027
entries.summary: The revised, simplified ESRS were published on 21 Sep 2026 and enter into force on 10 Nov 2026. They apply to financial years beginning on or after 1 Jan 2027. For FY2026, companies may choose between the previous ESRS, the new ESRS, or the previous ESRS with certain reliefs.
entries.whyItMatters: Directly affects our datapoint list, the KPI catalogue and the semantic models behind our reports. The FY2026 choice needs a decision soon.

entries.title: Voluntary Standard (VS) in force, replacing the VSME recommendation
entries.summary: The Voluntary Standard for companies outside CSRD scope entered into force on 24 Sep 2026. It replaces the previous recommendation to use the VSME, and it sets the reference for what in-scope companies may request from smaller value-chain partners.
entries.whyItMatters: Defines what we can reasonably ask from SME suppliers and what SME customers may ask from us. This is useful for designing supplier data requests.

entries.title: EFRAG consults on the draft XBRL taxonomy for the revised ESRS (until 11 Nov 2026)
entries.summary: EFRAG published the draft XBRL taxonomy for the revised ESRS on 17 Sep 2026, aligned with the 2026 draft list of datapoints. Feedback is due by 11 Nov 2026. Digital tagging is not yet mandatory, and ESMA will set binding ESEF requirements later.
entries.whyItMatters: The datapoint list and taxonomy are a natural backbone for our Fabric data model. Aligning column and measure names with them now saves rework when tagging becomes mandatory.

entries.title: Simplified EU Taxonomy reporting applies from FY2026: 10% materiality and ~64% fewer datapoints
entries.summary: The delegated act simplifying Taxonomy reporting was published on 8 Jan 2026 and applies from 1 Jan 2026. Non-financial companies need not assess activities that together make up less than 10% of turnover, CapEx or OpEx. Required datapoints fall by about 64%, and the pollution DNSH criteria are simplified.
entries.whyItMatters: Could significantly shrink our Taxonomy data collection and the related report pages for FY2026.

entries.title: EUDR applies from 30 Dec 2026; Commission confirms no further postponement
entries.summary: On 4 May 2026, the Commission published its EUDR simplification review: updated guidance and FAQs, a draft delegated act on product scope, and an updated information-system implementing act. Large and medium companies must comply from 30 Dec 2026. Micro and small operators outside the timber sector must comply from 30 Jun 2027.
entries.whyItMatters: Pulp and paper are wood-based products within the EUDR's scope; products made entirely from recovered material are generally excluded. Check the draft scope act for our product mix and our due diligence data flows (geolocation, supplier statements) before the December deadline.

entries.title: PPWR has applied since 12 Aug 2026; producer register implementing act still delayed
entries.summary: Conformity assessment, verification duties and most harmonised EPR rules apply from 12 Aug 2026. The Commission published guidance on 5 Jun 2026 and updated FAQs in August. The implementing act on national producer registers is delayed. Other obligations (labelling, recyclability, recycled content) follow in phases.
entries.whyItMatters: Packaging data (materials, recyclability, recycled content) will become a reporting and compliance dataset. It's a candidate for a dedicated Fabric data product.

entries.title: Empowering Consumers Directive: stricter green-claims rules apply since 27 Sep 2026
entries.summary: Generic claims such as "eco-friendly" are banned unless backed by recognised excellent environmental performance. Offset-based climate-neutral product claims are prohibited, and sustainability labels must be based on certification schemes or set by public authorities. The separate Green Claims Directive has been withdrawn.
entries.whyItMatters: Every product claim needs a traceable data basis. Our KPIs (e.g. recycled fibre share, product footprints) may increasingly be used to substantiate marketing claims.

entries.title: Commission proposes post-2030 EU ETS reform: slower cap decline, conditional free allocation
entries.summary: The proposal of 17 Jul 2026 lowers the linear reduction factor to 3.7% (2031–35) and 1.7% (2036–40) and halves the MSR intake rate to 12%. From 2031, free allocation would depend on approved decarbonisation investment plans (80% upfront, 20% at the end of each period). A separate proposal adds about €6bn in free allocation for 2026–2030. Parliament and Council negotiations follow.
entries.whyItMatters: Paper mills are ETS installations. This affects long-term CO₂ cost scenarios, free allocation planning and the link between our decarbonisation roadmap and allowances.

entries.title: ETS2 (buildings & road transport) postponed to 2028
entries.summary: Carbon pricing for fuels used in buildings and road transport under ETS2 will start in 2028 instead of 2027, as part of the EU 2040 climate deal.
entries.whyItMatters: Relevant for fuel cost scenarios in logistics and for Scope 1/3 transport emission costs.

entries.title: CBAM definitive period since 1 Jan 2026, with a 50-tonne de minimis threshold
entries.summary: The CBAM simplification replaced the €150 per-shipment rule with an annual 50-tonne threshold per importer. Certificates for 2026 imports are sold from Feb 2027, and the annual declaration deadline moves to 30 Sep. Pulp and paper are not CBAM goods.
entries.whyItMatters: Low direct relevance. It matters only if we import CBAM goods (e.g. steel, aluminium, fertiliser) above the threshold.

entries.title: SBTi Corporate Net-Zero Standard v2.0 published, mandatory from 31 Jan 2028
entries.summary: Version 2.0 shifts the focus from target setting to implementation. It expands target options across Scopes 1–3 with clearer Scope 3 rules and broader criteria for neutralising residual emissions, and companies must support carbon removals from 2035.
entries.whyItMatters: Affects how we track progress against targets (and which data we need for Scope 3) once targets are revalidated under v2.0.

entries.title: GHG Protocol Scope 2 revision: consultation closed, final rules pending
entries.summary: The public consultation closed on 31 Jan 2026. Proposals include hourly matching of renewable instruments, physical deliverability and unique claims. The current guidance remains valid until the final standard is published.
entries.whyItMatters: Hourly matching would require much more granular energy data (hourly consumption per site) in our data platform and could change market-based Scope 2 results.

entries.title: Fabric data agents generally available; Copilot Studio integration GA since Aug 2026
entries.summary: Fabric data agents were announced as GA at FabCon Atlanta (March 2026). Integration with Copilot Studio followed as GA in August 2026, so data agents can be used inside Copilot Studio agents and Teams.
entries.whyItMatters: We can now plan production data agents on our sustainability semantic models instead of pilots only.

entries.title: Fabric IQ in Microsoft 365 Copilot GA; Fabric IQ MCP server GA; ontology still in preview
entries.summary: Fabric IQ is the business-meaning layer over semantic models and graph. It reached GA in Microsoft 365 Copilot (announced at FabCon Europe, Barcelona), and the Fabric IQ MCP server reached GA in September 2026. The ontology feature remains in preview.
entries.whyItMatters: Opens a path for colleagues to query sustainability KPIs directly from M365 Copilot. Good definitions in our semantic models become even more important.

entries.title: Fabric Apps: build web apps on semantic models with governed write-back
entries.summary: Fabric Apps (announced at Build 2026) are a workspace item for browser-based apps with Entra authentication. Data apps query semantic models via DAX, and operational apps get a managed SQL database with GraphQL. Write-back data mirrors into OneLake. FabCon Europe added PostgreSQL, TypeScript backend functions and a Secret Store.
entries.whyItMatters: A potential replacement for Excel-based manual data collection (e.g. site questionnaires, target inputs) directly inside our Fabric domain.

entries.title: Agentic app creation in Power BI Desktop (preview)
entries.summary: Announced at FabCon Europe 2026 and rolling out in preview for Pro, PPU and Fabric capacity. Copilot can also generate real-time dashboards from text descriptions.
entries.whyItMatters: Could speed up prototyping of new report pages for non-technical team members.

entries.title: Foundry IQ GA; Foundry agents can use Fabric data agents via Toolboxes (preview)
entries.summary: At Build 2026, Foundry IQ became GA as the knowledge layer for Foundry agents (Fabric IQ, Work IQ, Azure SQL, files, MCP). Fabric IQ in Foundry, connecting agents to Fabric data agents, ontology and semantic models via Toolboxes, is in preview.
entries.whyItMatters: This is the bridge between our Fabric data agents and custom Foundry agents, e.g. a reporting assistant that combines KPIs with regulatory documents.

entries.title: Foundry Agent Service: publishing to Teams/M365 Copilot, scheduled 'Routines' and agent memory
entries.summary: Build 2026 announcements included publishing Foundry agents to Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot, Routines for scheduled or timer-based agent runs (preview), and procedural, user and session memory (preview). Multi-agent orchestration patterns in the Agent Framework are stable.
entries.whyItMatters: Routines could automate recurring tasks such as monthly KPI commentary or data-quality checks. Teams publishing makes agents easy for the team to reach.

entries.title: Microsoft Sustainability Manager 2026 wave 1: calculation versions, period locks, green ledger
entries.summary: Planned investments cover external reporting structure, multiple calculation versions with period locks, a green-ledger view connecting Dynamics 365 Finance, and Copilot agent experiences. Microsoft stops publishing release plans from Sep 2026, and new capabilities move to the AI at Work roadmap.
entries.whyItMatters: A useful benchmark of features for our own Fabric-based solution (versioned calculations, period locking), even if we don't use the product.

entries.title: Microsoft Learn: using a semantic model as a Fabric data agent source
entries.summary: Official guidance on connecting data agents to Power BI semantic models: prerequisites, how the agent generates DAX, and how to improve answers with 'Prep data for AI' (AI data schema, verified answers, AI instructions).
entries.whyItMatters: This is the starting point for our data agents on the sustainability semantic models.

entries.title: Prep data for AI vs. data agent instructions: what goes where
entries.summary: Explains which guidance belongs in the semantic model ('Prep data for AI') and which belongs in the data agent's instructions, to avoid duplication and contradictory behaviour.
entries.whyItMatters: Helps us set a team convention: KPI definitions in the model, conversation behaviour in the agent.

entries.title: How to write good AI instructions for a semantic model
entries.summary: Practical patterns for writing AI instructions on semantic models: terminology, default filters, measure preferences and what to avoid.
entries.whyItMatters: Our ESG terminology (Scope 1/2/3, market- vs location-based, site codes) needs explicit instructions for good agent answers.

entries.title: 5 best practices for deploying Microsoft Fabric data agents
entries.summary: Consulting perspective on scoping, data preparation, testing with real user questions, and governance when rolling out Fabric data agents.
entries.whyItMatters: Useful as a checklist before we put a data agent in front of the wider organisation.

entries.title: Microsoft Learn: consume a Fabric data agent from Microsoft Foundry
entries.summary: Official how-to for connecting a published Fabric data agent to a Foundry agent, including authentication and identity passthrough.
entries.whyItMatters: This is the technical path if we want Foundry agents to use our Fabric data while respecting users' access rights.

entries.title: Case study: Stolt-Nielsen turns CSRD compliance into sustainability insights
entries.summary: KPMG client story on building a CSRD reporting set-up that delivers management insights beyond compliance.
entries.whyItMatters: A peer example of positioning ESG controlling as steering support, not just reporting.

entries.title: Microsoft webinar: an 'ESG light' data model in Microsoft Fabric
entries.summary: On-demand session on a lightweight ESG data model built in Fabric, as an alternative to the full sustainability data solution.
entries.whyItMatters: A reference to compare with our own sustainability data domain design.
